column3: “If it is good in your eyes” is rendered “if you like,” and “money, the price of this” as “the price of it in money.”
“Far be it to me from the LORD” is rendered “The LORD forbid me.”
“If you are desiring” is rendered “if it pleases you.”
“Are you now doing kingship?” is rendered “Do you now reign?”, and “food” as “bread.”
“Sons of worthlessness” is rendered “worthless men,” and the euphemistic “blessed God” as “cursed God.”
“One who urinates on a wall” is rendered “every male,” and “shut up and freed” as “both bond and free.”
The Hebrew reads “rampart” (some manuscripts “portion”); NASB renders “district.”
Close to the Hebrew; NASB adds “because.”
“On his body” is not rendered, and “dejectedly” is rendered “despondently.”
